title: OSHA crane hoisting personnel practice questions
description: Free OSHA crane hoisting personnel practice questions on 29 CFR 1926.1431. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(a), who must demonstrate that conventional means of reaching the work area would be more hazardous, or are not possible, before equipment may be used to hoist employees?

options.A: The equipment operator
options.B: The employer
options.D: The employees to be hoisted

questions.explanation: "The use of equipment to hoist employees is prohibited except where the employer demonstrates that the erection, use, and dismantling of conventional means of reaching the work area ... would be more hazardous, or is not possible because of the project's structural design or worksite conditions."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The use of equipment to hoist employees is prohibited except where the employer demonstrates that the erection, use, and dismantling of conventional means of reaching the work area

questions.question: Which work does 29 CFR 1926.1431(a) say its restriction on using equipment to hoist employees does not apply to?

options.A: Work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection) of part 1926
options.B: Work covered by subpart V (Power Transmission and Distribution) of part 1926
options.D: Hoisting employees in chimney operations

questions.explanation: "This paragraph does not apply to work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection) of this part and also does not apply to routine personnel access to an underground worksite via shaft as covered by § 1926.800 (Underground Construction) of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: This paragraph does not apply to work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection) of this part

questions.question: What drill shaft diameter does 29 CFR 1926.1431(b)(2)(i) set for the exception under which a personnel platform is not required for hoisting employees into and out of drill shafts?

options.A: Up to and including 4 feet
options.B: Over 8 feet
options.D: Up to and including 12 feet

questions.explanation: A personnel platform is not required for hoisting employees "Into and out of drill shafts that are up to and including 8 feet in diameter", with paragraph (o) setting the requirements for hoisting these employees.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Into and out of drill shafts that are up to and including 8 feet in diameter

questions.question: 29 CFR 1926.1431(n) prohibits hoisting personnel near power lines at set distances. Which work is excepted from that prohibition?

options.A: Work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection)
options.B: Work in storage-tank operations
options.D: Work covered by subpart V (Power Transmission and Distribution)

questions.explanation: Hoisting personnel near power lines at those distances "is prohibited, except for work covered by subpart V of this part (Power Transmission and Distribution)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(c)(1), who must have determined that the footing the equipment is located on is sufficiently firm and stable?

options.A: A qualified person
options.B: The equipment operator
options.D: The signal person

questions.explanation: The equipment must be "located on footing that a qualified person has determined to be sufficiently firm and stable."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: located on footing that a qualified person has determined to be sufficiently firm and stable

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(d)(5)(vii), what must happen if a required device stops working properly during personnel hoisting operations?

options.A: The competent person may approve an alternative measure
options.B: The lift may continue if the signal person watches the boom
options.C: The operator must safely stop operations, and they must not resume until the device is again working properly
options.D: The current lift may be finished and the device tagged out afterward

questions.explanation: "If a device stops working properly during such operations, the operator must safely stop operations. Personnel hoisting operations must not resume until the device is again working properly. Alternative measures are not permitted."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If a device stops working properly during such operations, the operator must safely stop operations.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(d)(5), which equipment must be equipped with a properly functioning automatic overload protection device?

options.A: Derricks
options.B: Articulating cranes
options.D: Equipment with telescoping booms

questions.explanation: "Articulating cranes must be equipped with a properly functioning automatic overload protection device." Luffing jibs and telescoping booms have their own device requirements, and derricks are excluded from the variable angle boom list.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Articulating cranes must be equipped with a properly functioning automatic overload protection device.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(d)(5)(v), for which work does the rule's exception say the anti two-block device is not required when hoisting personnel?

options.A: Work covered by subpart R (Steel Erection)
options.B: Equipment that travels on fixed rails
options.C: Lifts with a boom-attached personnel platform
options.D: Pile driving operations

questions.explanation: "Exception: This device is not required when hoisting personnel in pile driving operations. Instead, paragraph (p)(2) of this section specifies how to prevent two-blocking during such operations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Exception: This device is not required when hoisting personnel in pile driving operations.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(e)(1), who must design the personnel platform and the attachment/suspension system used for hoisting personnel?

options.A: A competent person
options.B: The equipment manufacturer
options.D: A qualified person familiar with structural design

questions.explanation: "A qualified person familiar with structural design must design the personnel platform and attachment/suspension system used for hoisting personnel." A certified welder performs the welding under (e)(5).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A qualified person familiar with structural design must design the personnel platform and attachment/suspension system used for hoisting personnel.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(e)(8)(i), when may a personnel platform's access gate/door swing outward?

options.A: Whenever the gate is equipped with a latch
options.B: When, due to the size of the platform, such as a 1-person platform, it is infeasible for the door to swing inward and allow safe entry
options.D: When a competent person approves it at the pre-lift meeting

questions.explanation: "If due to the size of the personnel platform, such as a 1-person platform, it is infeasible for the door to swing inward and allow safe entry for the platform occupant, then the access gate/door may swing outward."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: If due to the size of the personnel platform, such as a 1-person platform, it is infeasible for the door to swing inward and allow safe entry for the platform occupant, then the access gate/door may swing outward.

questions.question: What does 29 CFR 1926.1431(g)(5) say about the past use of the bridles and associated rigging that suspend the personnel platform?

options.A: They must not have been used for any purpose other than hoisting personnel
options.B: They may have been used for materials if proof tested
options.C: They must be new for each jobsite
options.D: They may have been used for any lift within their rated capacity

questions.explanation: "The bridles and associated rigging must not have been used for any purpose other than hoisting personnel."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The bridles and associated rigging must not have been used for any purpose other than hoisting personnel.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(g)(1)(ii), what must shackles used in place of hooks be?

options.A: Of any type rated for five times the load
options.B: Of the round pin type without a retaining pin
options.C: Of the alloy anchor type, with either a bolt, nut and retaining pin in place, or of the screw type with the screw pin secured from accidental removal
options.D: Of the type approved by the signal person

questions.explanation: "Shackles used in place of hooks must be of the alloy anchor type, with either" a bolt, nut and retaining pin in place, or "Of the screw type, with the screw pin secured from accidental removal."

questions.topic: Trial lift, inspection and proof testing
questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(h)(2)(ii), when is a repeat trial lift not required after the lift route is changed?

options.A: When the competent person determines that the new route presents no new factors affecting safety
options.B: When the operator has used the new route before
options.C: When the change happens within the same shift
options.D: When the proof test has already been passed

questions.explanation: The trial lift must be repeated when "The lift route is changed, unless the competent person determines that the new route presents no new factors affecting safety."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The lift route is changed, unless the competent person determines that the new route presents no new factors affecting safety.

questions.topic: Trial lift, inspection and proof testing
questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(j)(1), when must the personnel platform and rigging be proof tested?

options.A: Once every 12 months
options.B: Before each shift in which personnel will be hoisted
options.C: Only when the platform is new
options.D: At each jobsite, prior to hoisting employees on the platform, and after any repair or modification

questions.explanation: "At each jobsite, prior to hoisting employees on the personnel platform, and after any repair or modification, the platform and rigging must be proof tested to 125 percent of the platform's rated capacity." Before each shift is the timing for the trial lift, not the proof test.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: At each jobsite, prior to hoisting employees on the personnel platform, and after any repair or modification, the platform and rigging must be proof tested

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(k)(8)(i), when wind speed (sustained or gusts) exceeds 20 mph at the personnel platform, who must determine whether it is not safe to lift personnel?

options.A: The equipment operator
options.B: The signal person
options.D: The person responsible for the task

questions.explanation: "When wind speed (sustained or gusts) exceeds 20 mph at the personnel platform, a qualified person must determine if, in light of the wind conditions, it is not safe to lift personnel."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: a qualified person must determine if, in light of the wind conditions, it is not safe to lift personnel

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(m)(2), who must attend the pre-lift meeting?

options.A: The equipment operator and the competent person only
options.B: The equipment operator, signal person (if used for the lift), employees to be hoisted, and the person responsible for the task to be performed
options.C: The employees to be hoisted and the qualified person who designed the platform
options.D: The controlling entity and the equipment owner

questions.explanation: A pre-lift meeting must be "Attended by the equipment operator, signal person (if used for the lift), employees to be hoisted, and the person responsible for the task to be performed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Attended by the equipment operator, signal person (if used for the lift), employees to be hoisted, and the person responsible for the task to be performed.

questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(k)(10)(i), except over water, where must the personal fall arrest system of employees occupying the personnel platform be attached?

options.A: To the lower load block
options.B: To the structure where the work is to be performed
options.D: To a structural member within the personnel platform

questions.explanation: "Except over water, employees occupying the personnel platform must be provided and use a personal fall arrest system. The system must be attached to a structural member within the personnel platform."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1431, Hoisting personnel (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The system must be attached to a structural member within the personnel platform.

questions.topic: Drill shafts, pile driving, marine and tank operations
questions.question: When an employee is hoisted on a boatswain's chair into or out of a drill shaft under 29 CFR 1926.1431(o)(3), where must a signal person be stationed?

options.A: At the shaft opening
options.B: At the equipment controls
options.D: At the boom tip

questions.explanation: "A signal person must be stationed at the shaft opening."

options.A: A full body harness attached to the overhaul ball
options.B: A U.S. Coast Guard personal flotation device approved for industrial use
options.C: A hard hat with a chin strap only
options.D: A harness attached to the transfer device

questions.explanation: "Each employee must wear a U.S. Coast Guard personal flotation device approved for industrial use."

questions.topic: Drill shafts, pile driving, marine and tank operations
questions.question: Under 29 CFR 1926.1431(s)(1), in storage-tank, shaft and chimney operations, when must a boatswain's chair be used instead of a personnel platform?

options.A: When the operator prefers it
options.B: When only one employee is hoisted
options.C: When the employer can demonstrate that use of a personnel platform is infeasible
options.D: When the wind exceeds 20 mph

questions.explanation: "The employee must be in a personnel platform except when the employer can demonstrate that use of a personnel platform is infeasible; in such a case, a boatswain's chair must be used."
